## summary
Worktree was cut from 683f272 (lacked 1a45970), so it was reset to 1a45970 first; node_modules junctioned.

FILES
- portal/scripts/inventory-surface.ts (new): parses src/server/actions/*.ts and src/app/api/**/route.ts, lists every exported function / HTTP method with the guard it reaches ("actionViewer(<perm>)", "actionViewer()", "apiViewer(<perm>)", "getViewer()", "getSession()", "public"); follows one level of same-file delegation (signPolicyAction→signPolicy, drill route answer(), auth wrappers). Exports inventory(); `npx tsx scripts/inventory-surface.ts` rewrites tests/fixtures/surface.json.
- portal/tests/fixtures/surface.json (new): 150 entries (133 actions, 17 route methods).
- portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts (new): two organisations A and B via tests/helpers/db.ts, each with an administrator and a learner viewer and a row in every tenant-scoped table (department, own module+lessons, assignment, policy+version+signoff, usb campaign+recipient, drill run, threat report, loop, material, incident, intel threat/policy, ticket, feedback, problem, path, live session+registration, report schedule, sandbox analysis, failed outbox mail, watermark code, module progress, notification). Table ROWS keyed by inventory entry: `run` rows call the action/route as A's admin with B's ids/slugs/tokens (and again as A's learner when the guard names a permission), `lower` rows (no foreign input but permission-guarded) call as the learner, `na` rows document why an entry is not tenant-scoped (self-service, public token routes by design, public auth/site). Refusal = undefined / 401-403-404 / FORBIDDEN-UNAUTHENTICATED thrown / ok:false / error / count 0; rows whose action legitimately filters foreign ids (createIncidentAction, createMaterialAction with B's people+department; reports route with ?d=B's department) assert the filtered outcome inline (empty audience, no B email in the CSV). Before/after each row a snapshot of every row of B across all 52 pgTables (by tenant_id, else user_id/module_id/lesson_id/policy_id/version_id/session_id/ticket_id/material_id/campaign_id/loop_id) must be identical. Two meta tests: inventory() must equal surface.json, and ROWS keys must equal the fixture keys. Fixture tenants are enterprise_hrm with the seed-only live_drill override and email enabled so feature gates pass and the tenant predicate is what refuses. Mocks mirror the real actionViewer/allowed semantics (two-step verification not under test).
- portal/src/server/tutor.ts + src/app/api/tutor/route.ts + schema.ts comment (S-10): tutorCacheId(tenantId, locale, lessonId, sceneId, question, contentLocale, scenes) — tenant id is the first key component; the wave-A lesson-text hash stays; existing 365-day cleanup in jobs.ts:395 unchanged. tests/tutor.test.ts updated; tests/tutor-cache.test.ts (new) mocks @anthropic-ai/sdk with a finishing stream and asserts ai → cache for A, ai again for B, and two tutor_cache rows with distinct ids/tenantIds for one library lesson.
- portal/src/server/actions/learning.ts (S-11 c): lessonOf() (shared by start, reach and complete) refuses a non-string or >100-char slug/lessonKey before any query; the module-membership query already existed in wave A (lessonOf resolves the key against the module's lessons; recorded as such). Test appended to learning-actions.test.ts: foreign key, 101-char key and 101-char slug write no module/lesson progress; the real key records lastLessonKey.
- portal/src/app/api/admin/policies/[id]/signoffs/route.ts (S-11 d): `showIp = can(v.user.role, "audit.read")`; the IP header and value are emitted only then. tests/signoffs-route.test.ts (new): tenant_admin gets the IP column with 203.0.113.7, content_creator gets the same CSV without the column and without the address.

LEAKS FOUND: none. Every tenant-scoped action and route refused B's ids as A's admin and the lower role, and B's rows never changed (152/152 tests). Notes for the register: assignIncidentTrainingAction, remindPeopleAction, remindPolicyAction, resendFailedMailAction and remindAwaitingAction answer ok with count 0 for foreign ids (nothing happens; treated as "empty"); savePathAction with a foreign sourceId silently creates an own path from the submitted texts (no data of B copied; the row probes id and moduleSlugs instead).

RLS EVALUATION (for the ADR): PostgreSQL RLS would need (1) `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and `CREATE POLICY … USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid) WITH CHECK (same)` on the 34 tables with tenant_id, with `tenant_id IS NULL OR …` on modules, learning_paths and outbox (library/platform rows); (2) the ~12 child tables keyed by user/module/lesson/policy/version/session/ticket/material/campaign/loop (module_progress, lesson_progress, lessons, lesson_contents, ai_cache, policy_versions, policy_signoffs, session_registrations, ticket_messages, material_decisions, campaign_recipients, loop_events) either get an additive tenant_id column (backfilled by migration) or EXISTS-subquery policies, which cost a join per statement; (3) platform-wide tables (tenants, demo_requests, rate_limit_buckets, login_attempts, job_ticks, outbox with null tenant) and the operator console (/super, platform.ts, super/demo-requests) and jobs.ts (cross-tenant ticks, cleanup, reminders) need a bypass role or per-tenant transactions; (4) the application side is the XL part: src/server/db exposes a module-level db() singleton over a pool, and SET LOCAL is per transaction, so every page render, server action, route handler and job tick must open a transaction and run `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` before its first query — a per-request db bound through AsyncLocalStorage or a wrapper on every requireViewer/actionViewer/apiViewer caller — while the viewer lookup itself (sessions→users→tenants) runs before the tenant is known and must bypass the policy; (5) docker-compose must add a non-owner application role (RLS is ignored by superusers/BYPASSRLS and by the table owner unless FORCE), migrations keep running as the owner, so two connection strings; (6) PGlite in tests is real Postgres and can hold the policies, but tests/helpers/db.ts would have to SET ROLE / set app.tenant_id per statement in every DB-backed test file, and a test that forgets it reads nothing. Risk: RLS silently does nothing when the app connects as the owner without FORCE. Verdict: the generated suite is executable, regenerable evidence that every entry point refuses another organisation's ids and writes nothing of it, and it blocks new unguarded endpoints at CI time; it satisfies due diligence for application-layer isolation. RLS stays a defence-in-depth layer worth its XL cost only where a contract requires database-level isolation; if so, the order is additive tenant_id on child tables, then FORCE RLS with a per-request transaction wrapper.

PROGRESS LINE: B3-isolation: generated cross-organisation/lower-role suite over all 150 actions and route methods (inventory-checked, no leak found); tutor cache per organisation; lesson key/slug capped at 100; sign-off IP column only for audit.read; RLS evaluated and deferred.

## left_open
Owner questions: (1) S-03: do enterprise/government buyers require database-level RLS contractually, or does the automated cross-organisation suite satisfy due diligence (the RLS path is XL: per-request transactions around the db() singleton, a non-owner role in docker-compose, tenant_id on ~12 child tables)? (2) S-10: accept that every organisation now pays for its own first tutor answer per question on shared library lessons (more Anthropic calls), or moderate answers before caching and share them instead? Existing tutor_cache rows keyed without a tenant are orphaned until the 365-day cleanup removes them (a one-off `delete from tutor_cache` at deploy frees the space sooner). Not done: the full vitest suite (orchestrator runs it after the merge); only the touched/added files were run (186 tests). Risk to know: cross-tenant.test.ts takes ~30 s (152 tests, 52-table snapshot per row) and treats `count: 0` answers as refusals; a future action that answers ok:true with a foreign id but writes nothing of B still passes only if it also reports count 0, otherwise its row must assert inline. Skipped: no new dependencies, no schema change, docs/build files untouched as instructed.

- [major] portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts:478 The lower-role pass never actually tests the role gate on `run` rows. When the guard names a permission, the row runs again as A's learner but still with B's ids, and `refused()` accepts any refusal: ok:false, error, 404, count 0. If an actionViewer("people.write") / apiViewer(...) gate were dropped or weakened, the call would still be refused by the tenant predicate on B's ids and the row would pass. That covers about 80 entries. So the acceptance item about a lower role, and the summary's claim that no role leak exists, are not backed by any assertion that could fail for those entries. Only the `lower` rows test the role gate in isolation. -> In the learner pass of permission-guarded entries, require the gate's own refusal and not just any refusal: for actionViewer(<perm>) the settled result must be Error("FORBIDDEN"), and for apiViewer(<perm>) a Response with status 403. The gate runs before any lookup, so this isolates the role check even with B's ids. One small helper next to refused(); add per-row exceptions only where an input check legitimately runs before the gate.
- [minor] portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts:184 snapshot() uses only the first key column a table has, and userId comes before moduleId, lessonId, sessionId and the rest. Rows that A's own user writes against B's objects therefore never show up in B's snapshot: moduleProgress(userId=A, moduleId=B) and lessonProgress(userId=A, lessonId=B) are examples. startLessonAction and reachSceneAction return void, so refused(undefined) is always true. Together that makes those two rows vacuous: a regression that let A's people record progress on B's custom module would pass. -> Build the snapshot's where clause as an OR over every key column the table has (tenantId, userId in B's users, moduleId = B's module, lessonId in B's lessons, sessionId, …), or add inline assertions to the two void rows that no module_progress or lesson_progress row exists for B's module or lessons.
- [minor] portal/scripts/inventory-surface.ts:22 The inventory only recognises `export (async) function name`. A future action written as `export const fooAction = async (...) =>`, or re-exported with `export { … } from`, would be missing from both the inventory and surface.json. The completeness meta-test would stay green, which defeats the guarantee that a new action cannot land without a row. -> In the meta-test (or the script), import each src/server/actions/*.ts module and each route module and compare their exported function names with the inventory keys, or make the script fail on any other `export const`/`export {` form that resolves to a function.
- [minor] portal/tests/fixtures/surface.json: Entries that gate with allowed() after getViewer() or a bare actionViewer() are recorded as "getViewer()" / "actionViewer()". Examples are api/sandbox/[id]/stix:GET (secops.read), escalateAnalysisAction (secops.read), replyTicketAction (support.manage branch) and api/admin/people/[kind]:GET (people.read). PERMISSION.test() fails for them, so their `run` rows never run as the learner and the role half of the acceptance is skipped for them. -> Have guardOf also detect `allowed(v, "<perm>")` in the function body and record it (for example "getViewer()+allowed(secops.read)"), and extend the PERMISSION regex to match it, so those rows get the learner pass.
- [nit] portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts: No row has a positive control. A row can be refused for a reason unrelated to the tenant (invalid input, wrong state, missing feature) and still pass, so the suite cannot show that the tenant predicate is what refused it. -> For a representative sample, or cheaply for every `run` row whose input is symmetric, run the same call with A's own ids as A's admin in a throwaway organisation and expect success. Alternatively, document per row why the input is valid.

## fix
fixed:
[major] portal/scripts/inventory-surface.ts: server-action files are now found by directive, not folder. inventory() walks src/** (readdirSync recursive) and includes every .ts/.tsx whose first statement is "use server", keyed by the path relative to src (server/actions/people.addPersonAction, app/(focus)/learn/[slug]/[lessonId]/actions.loadCaptionsAction, server/lab/vm-action.completeVmLabAction). Fixture regenerated (152 entries); the 131 action keys in the test table were renamed to the server/actions/ prefix; two rows added: loadCaptionsAction run as A with B's lesson id and locale az expecting null (with a positive control first: B's own administrator gets a non-null caption map, so the null is the reach filter and not a missing translation; org() gives B's first lesson an az lesson_contents row for that), completeVmLabAction as na: SELF.
[major] portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts: the learner pass now requires the gate's own refusal. GATE = /^(actionViewer|apiViewer)\(\w/ selects entries whose gate names a permission; for those, each result of the learner pass (run rows re-run as A's learner with B's ids, and lower rows) must satisfy gateRefused(): Error("FORBIDDEN") for actionViewer(<perm>), Response 403 for apiViewer(<perm>). Entries where the permission comes only from a later allowed() keep the loose refused(). Verified live: with gateRefused forced to false, 99 of 154 tests fail; restored, 154 pass. No per-row exception was needed (every guarded entry calls its gate before any input check).
[minor] portal/scripts/inventory-surface.ts: checkExports() throws on any top-level `export` line that is not `export type`/`export interface`/`export [async] function NAME` (for route files the Next.js segment-config `export const dynamic|dynamicParams|revalidate|fetchCache|runtime|preferredRegion|maxDuration` is allowed), so `export const GET = withX(...)`, `export { GET as HEAD }`, `export default` and `export const fooAction = async () =>` fail the inventory (and thus the fixture test) instead of shipping unlisted. A route file that exports none of the recognised methods also throws. Covers findings 3 and 6 together.
[minor] portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts snapshot(): the where clause is now or() over every key column the table has (tenantId, userId in B's users, moduleId = B's module, lessonId in B's lessons, policyId, versionId, sessionId, ticketId, materialId, campaignId, loopId) instead of the first one found, so module_progress(userId=A, moduleId=B) and lesson_progress(userId=A, lessonId=B) rows are part of B's snapshot. That makes the void startLessonAction and reachSceneAction rows non-vacuous: a leak that recorded A's progress on B's module or lessons changes the snapshot and fails the row. Covers findings 4 and 5 (finding 4's inline-assertion alternative was therefore not needed).
[minor] portal/scripts/inventory-surface.ts guardOf(): when the function's own body (or the reached function's) contains allowed(v, "<perm>") after its gate, the guard is recorded as "<gate>+allowed(<perm>)" (e.g. api/sandbox/[id]/stix:GET = getViewer()+allowed(secops.read), server/actions/security.escalateAnalysisAction = actionViewer()+allowed(secops.read), server/actions/engage.replyTicketAction = actionViewer()+allowed(support.manage), api/admin/people/[kind]:GET = getViewer()+allowed(people.read), plus api/admin/reports/[kind]:GET, api/subtitles:POST, api/tutor:POST, reports.saveScheduleAction, reports.removeScheduleAction, api/health:GET, api/sso/start:GET). The test's PERMISSION regex is now /\(\w/ so those entries get the learner pass (loose refused(), since their role check runs after a tenant lookup).
